items.title: How names begin

items.prose: Prove that normalised counts are the maximum likelihood estimate for one row of $K$ outcomes.
items.question: Put the steps in order and leave out the step that does not belong.

lines.text: A row of counts $n_1, \dots, n_K$ with total $n$ has log-likelihood $\sum_k n_k \ln q_k$ under chances $q$.
Divide by $n$: it is $n \sum_k \hat p_k \ln q_k$ with $\hat p_k = n_k / n$.
So it equals $-n\,\big(H(\hat p) + D(\hat p \,\|\, q)\big)$, since $-\sum_k \hat p_k \ln q_k$ is the cross-entropy $H(\hat p, q)$.
$H(\hat p)$ is fixed by the data, so only $D(\hat p \,\|\, q)$ changes with $q$.
By Jensen (info l6), $D \ge 0$, and $D = 0$ only at $q = \hat p$; so $q = \hat p$ is the unique maximum.
Since $\ln$ is increasing, the best $q$ puts all its chance on the largest count.
lines.why: Putting all chance on one outcome gives every other observed outcome $\ln 0 = -\infty$; the log of a product is a sum over all the counts.

feedback.correct: The log-likelihood is $-n$ times a cross-entropy, maximised only where the KL term vanishes.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Each step needs the one before it.

byKey.hx: That step ignores the other counts: any outcome given chance 0 costs $-\infty$.

explain.text: The log-likelihood is $-n(H(\hat p) + D(\hat p \| q))$. Only the KL term depends on $q$, and it is 0 only at $q = \hat p$.

items.title: Logits as log counts
Why the network cannot win
items.prompt: A one-layer network on one-hot letters is trained on some names. Explain why it can never score a lower average loss on those same names than the normalised count table, and say what would have to change for a network to beat it. Use the language of likelihood and cross-entropy.
items.model:
With a one-hot input, the network's output for input $a$ depends only on row $a$ of $W$: $\operatorname{softmax}(W_a)$. So whatever the weights, the network is a table of 27 rows of chances, one row per current symbol.

The average loss on the training names splits by row: $L = \frac{1}{n}\sum_a N_a\, H(\hat p_a, q_a)$, where $\hat p_a$ is row $a$ of the normalised counts and $q_a$ the model's row. Each term is $N_a\big(H(\hat p_a) + D(\hat p_a \| q_a)\big)$, and $D \ge 0$ with equality only at $q_a = \hat p_a$. So the least possible loss is $\frac{1}{n}\sum_a N_a H(\hat p_a)$, reached by the counts: 2.3820 on the 500-name subset.

The network can approach that floor (2.4122 after 100 steps, 2.3830 after 3,000) but never pass it. It cannot even reach it exactly where a count is 0, since softmax never gives a chance of 0. To beat the counts it needs more input: a context of several letters, so that it is no longer a 27-row table. That is the MLP of level 2. A network can also do better on new names than an unsmoothed table, but that is a held-out question, not one about the training names.

rubric.text: Says the output depends only on one row of $W$, so the network is a 27-row table of chances
Writes the training loss as a sum over rows of $N_a H(\hat p_a, q_a)$ (or as average negative log-likelihood)
Uses $H = H(\hat p) + D(\hat p \| q)$ with $D \ge 0$, equal to 0 only at $q = \hat p$
Concludes the counts are the floor; quotes 2.3820 or the curve approaching it
Notes zero counts: softmax never reaches chance 0, so the floor is approached, not reached
Says what would change it: more context in the input (or another question, held-out loss)
